translationRepairs: On the gengchen new moon in the third month of spring, Guangshun 3, Bai Chongzan (acting Xiangzhou) was appointed Huazhou military governor; Wang Jin (Zhengzhou) took Xiangzhou; former Yanzhou defense commissioner Suo Wanjin took Yanzhou; and Bozhou's Zhang Duo took Tongzhou.

On the gengchen new moon in the third month of spring, Guangshun 3, Bai Chongzan (acting Xiangzhou) was appointed Huazhou military governor; Wang Jin (Zhengzhou) took Xiangzhou; former Yanzhou defense commissioner Suo Wanjin took Yan Prefecture (Yanzhou); and Bozhou's Zhang Duo took Tongzhou.
The original collapses 兗州 and 延州 into one Yanzhou posting. The replacement keeps former Yanzhou for 兗州 and names the new post Yan Prefecture, which is accurate English for 延州.

In spring of Guangshun year 3, third month, gengchen new moon: Bai Chongzan, acting commissioner of Xiangzhou, was made military governor of Huazhou; Wang Jin, defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, was made military governor of Xiangzhou; Suo Wanjin, former defense commissioner of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Yanzhou; and Zhang Duo, defense commissioner of Bozhou, was made military governor of Tongzhou.

In spring of Guangshun year 3, third month, gengchen new moon: Bai Chongzan, acting commissioner of Xiangzhou, was made military governor of Huazhou; Wang Jin, defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, was made military governor of Xiangzhou; Suo Wanjin, former defense commissioner of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Yan Prefecture; and Zhang Duo, defense commissioner of Bozhou, was made military governor of Tongzhou.
The literal repeats Yanzhou for both 兗州 and 延州, which is a real error. The proposed parenthetical Chinese is not allowed in the English field; Yan Prefecture is the English name for the 延州 post.
On jiashen Prince Rong, Cangzhou military governor, was named Kaifeng mayor and merit commissioner, enfeoffed Prince of Jin, with orders to schedule his formal investiture.
On jiashen Prince Rong, Chanzhou military governor, was named Kaifeng mayor and merit commissioner, enfeoffed Prince of Jin, with orders to schedule his formal investiture.
澶州 is Chanzhou; Cangzhou would be 滄州. The replacement restores the prefecture Rong held before the Kaifeng appointment.

On jiashen, the imperial son Rong, military governor of Cangzhou, was made Mayor of Kaifeng and concurrently Merit Commissioner, enfeoffed as Prince of Jin, and the responsible offices were ordered to choose a day and prepare the ritual investiture.

On jiashen, the imperial son Rong, military governor of Chanzhou, was made Mayor of Kaifeng and concurrently Merit Commissioner, enfeoffed as Prince of Jin, and the responsible offices were ordered to choose a day and prepare the ritual investiture.
The same 澶州 is mistranslated as Cangzhou in the literal field. Chanzhou is the correct English place name.

On bingxu Zheng Renhui (Northern Palace Secretariat and vice military affairs commissioner) took Cangzhou; Palace Front commander Li Chongjin took Sizhou; and reception commissioner Xiang Xun became inner reception commissioner.

On bingxu Zheng Renhui (Northern Palace Secretariat and vice military affairs commissioner) took Chanzhou; Palace Front commander Li Chongjin took Sizhou; and reception commissioner Xiang Xun became inner reception commissioner.
Zheng Renhui is made 澶州節度使, succeeding to Chanzhou, not Cangzhou.

On bingxu, Zheng Renhui, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made military governor of Cangzhou; Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, was given charge of Sizhou as defense commissioner; and Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, was made commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau.

On bingxu, Zheng Renhui, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made military governor of Chanzhou; Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, was given charge of Sizhou as defense commissioner; and Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, was made commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau.
The literal likewise renders 澶州 as Cangzhou. The replacement matches the Chinese posting.
On gengyin, Yan Yan, academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of War in the Ministry of Personnel, was removed from office and retained only his original post.
On gengyin, Yan Yan, academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of War, was stripped of his concurrent academician post and retained only his original office.
尚書兵部侍郎 is Vice Minister of War, not Personnel. 落職守本官 strips the concurrent Duanming academician post while keeping the vice-ministry.
On xinsi former Qingzhou prefect Guo Yanqin was ordered home.
On xinsi former Qing Prefecture (Qingzhou) prefect Guo Yanqin was ordered home.
慶州 is not 青州. The original Qingzhou conflates them; Qing Prefecture is accurate English for this posting.
Early in the dynasty Yanqin had been reassigned to Qingzhou and also ran the salt monopoly; he raised monopoly fees on his own authority, stirring resentment among both settlers and tribes.

Early in the dynasty Yanqin had been reassigned to Qing Prefecture (Qingzhou) and also ran the salt monopoly; he raised monopoly fees on his own authority, stirring resentment among both settlers and tribes.
再刺慶州 is a posting to Qing Prefecture, not Shandong Qingzhou. The replacement restores that distinction in English.

On guichou former Kaifeng mayor and Duke of Chu Hou Yi became grand mentor of the heir apparent; former Luoyang regent and Duke of Ju Wang Shouen took the Left Guards; and former Yongxing military governor Li Hongxin took the Left Martial Guards.

On guichou former Kaifeng mayor and Duke of Chu Hou Yi became grand mentor of the heir apparent; former Luoyang regent and Duke of Ju Wang Shouen was made General of the Left Guards; and former Yongxing military governor Li Hongxin was made General of the Left Martial Guards.
左衛上將軍 and 左武衛上將軍 are senior generalships. 'Took the Left Guards/Martial Guards' drops the rank; the replacement matches the chapter's own literal rendering.
On jiayin Left Guards general Song Yanyun became junior mentor of the heir apparent; junior mentor Yang Ningshi retired as right vice director of personnel.
On jiayin Left Guards general Song Yanyun became junior mentor of the heir apparent; junior mentor Yang Ningshi retired as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
尚書右僕射 is Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, not of the Ministry of Personnel.

On jiayin, Song Yanyun, General of the Left Guards, was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; Yang Ningshi, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and retired.

On jiayin, Song Yanyun, General of the Left Guards, was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; Yang Ningshi, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and retired.
The literal makes the same 吏部 error for 尚書右僕射. The replacement names the Shangshu office correctly.
On guimao heir-apparent guest Ma Yisun died.
On guiwei heir-apparent guest Ma Yisun died.
The date is 癸未 (guiwei). Guimao would be 癸卯; after 戊寅朔 the next dated event is 癸未, then 甲申.
On guimao, Ma Yisun, Guest of the Heir Apparent, died.
On guiwei, Ma Yisun, Guest of the Heir Apparent, died.
The literal repeats the same sexagenary mistranscription of 癸未 as guimao.
On jiashen Yedu regent Wang Yin petitioned three times for an audience and was granted permission.
On jiashen Wang Yin of Yedu petitioned three times for an audience and was granted permission.
鄴都王殷 identifies Wang Yin of Yedu. This sentence does not name a regency; 'regent' is added English.

On yiwei, Bian Guangfan, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Rites; Zhang Xu, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Censor-in-Chief; and Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-chief and Vice Minister of Rites in the Ministry of Personnel, was made Vice Minister of Justice to fill the post.

On yiwei, Bian Guangfan, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Rites; Zhang Xu, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Censor-in-Chief; and Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-chief and Vice Minister of Rites of the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Minister of Justice to fill the post.
尚書禮部侍郎 is Vice Minister of Rites in the Department of State Affairs, not an office of the Ministry of Personnel.
Zhengzhou Kaifeng Road commander Zhang Wanyou was also at Yueshou but did not join the mutiny.
Zhengzhou Kaidao (Open Road) commander Zhang Wanyou was also at Yueshou but did not join the mutiny.
開道指揮使 is the Kaidao directing-commander title, not a Kaifeng (開封) road command.
The court urgently dispatched palace attendant Ma E to investigate; E then joined with Wanyou to seize Yanzhang and thirteen others and behead them; the rest fled to Qizhou.
The court urgently dispatched palace attendant Ma E to investigate; E then joined with Wanyou to seize Yanzhang and thirteen men in all and behead them; the rest fled to Qizhou.
彥章等十三人 is a group of thirteen including Yanzhang. 'Thirteen others' would make fourteen; the idiomatic field already counts twelve others.

On gengxu former Tongzhou military governor Xue Huairang took the Left Encampment Guards; personnel vice director and education director Tian Min became acting director of imperial sacrifices; and Minister of Rites Wang Yi became acting Minister of War.

On gengxu former Tongzhou military governor Xue Huairang took the Left Encampment Guards; Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent overseer of the Directorate of Education Tian Min became acting director of imperial sacrifices; and Minister of Rites Wang Yi became acting Minister of War.
尚書左丞 is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, not a personnel vice director; 兼判國子監 is the concurrent education overseership.

Feng Dao (director of the Secretariat) headed the southern suburbs rites; Prince of Jin and Kaifeng mayor Rong managed the procession; acting Minister of War Wang Yi oversaw armor guards; censor-in-chief Zhang Xu oversaw ceremonial arms; acting sacrifices director Tian Min handled ritual; and former Yingzhou defense commissioner Guo Qiong served as acting imperial clan director.

Feng Dao (director of the Secretariat) headed the southern suburbs rites; Prince of Jin and Kaifeng mayor Rong managed the procession; acting Minister of War Wang Yi oversaw the imperial insignia cortege; censor-in-chief Zhang Xu oversaw ceremonial arms; acting sacrifices director Tian Min handled ritual; and former Yingzhou defense commissioner Guo Qiong served as acting imperial clan director.
鹵簿使 oversees the imperial insignia cortege, not armor guards, which would be a different ceremonial charge.
On bingyin the ritual commissioner proposed that Prince of Jin Rong serve as secondary offerer and also oversee the final offering when the emperor performed suburban and temple rites."
On bingyin the ritual commissioner proposed that Prince of Jin Rong serve as secondary offerer and also oversee the final offering when the emperor performed suburban and temple rites.
The idiomatic sentence is narrative summary, not a closed quotation. The stray final quotation mark is not in the Chinese wording outside the memorial.

On gengchen an order named Prince of Jin and Kaifeng mayor Rong Commissioner with Protocol of the Three Excellencies, acting Grand General, and concurrent palace attendant, continuing as Kaifeng mayor and merit commissioner with authority over all military affairs.

On gengchen an order named Prince of Jin and Kaifeng mayor Rong Commissioner with Protocol of the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent palace attendant, continuing as Kaifeng mayor and merit commissioner with authority over all military affairs.
檢校太尉 is Acting Grand Commandant. Grand General would be a different title (將軍/大將軍).

On gengchen, an order declared that the imperial son, Mayor of Kaifeng and Prince of Jin Rong, was approved as Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, Acting Grand General, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, acting as Mayor of Kaifeng and Merit Commissioner, with jurisdiction over internal and external military affairs.

On gengchen, an order declared that the imperial son, Mayor of Kaifeng and Prince of Jin Rong, was approved as Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, acting as Mayor of Kaifeng and Merit Commissioner, with jurisdiction over internal and external military affairs.
The literal makes the same 太尉/Grand General error. Commandant matches 太尉.

On jiashen Zhao Hui of Songzhou became Duke of Han; Chang Si of Qingzhou, Duke of Lai; Wang Yan of Xuzhou, Duke of Teng; Hou Zhang of Dengzhou, Duke of Shen; Wu Xingde of Luoyang, Duke of Qiao; Guo Congyi of Xuzhou was made acting grand preceptor; Wang Jing of Fengxiang, Duke of Bao; and Sun Fangjian of Huazhou, Duke of Xiao.

On jiashen Zhao Hui of Songzhou became Duke of Han; Chang Si of Qingzhou, Duke of Lai; Wang Yan of Xuzhou, Duke of Teng; Hou Zhang of Dengzhou, Duke of Shen; Wu Xingde of Luoyang, Duke of Qiao; Guo Congyi of Xu Prefecture was made acting grand preceptor; Wang Jing of Fengxiang, Duke of Bao; and Sun Fangjian of Huazhou, Duke of Xiao.
許州郭從義 is Xu Prefecture. Xuzhou in the same sentence already renders 徐州王晏, so the original collapses two prefectures.

On jiashen, Zhao Hui of Songzhou was advanced to Duke of Han; Chang Si of Qingzhou to Duke of Lai; Wang Yan of Xuzhou to Duke of Teng; Hou Zhang of Dengzhou to Duke of Shen; Wu Xingde of the Western Capital to Duke of Qiao; Guo Congyi of Xuzhou was made Acting Grand Preceptor; Wang Jing of Fengxiang was advanced to Duke of Bao; and Sun Fangjian of Huazhou to Duke of Xiao.

On jiashen, Zhao Hui of Songzhou was advanced to Duke of Han; Chang Si of Qingzhou to Duke of Lai; Wang Yan of Xuzhou to Duke of Teng; Hou Zhang of Dengzhou to Duke of Shen; Wu Xingde of the Western Capital to Duke of Qiao; Guo Congyi of Xu Prefecture was made Acting Grand Preceptor; Wang Jing of Fengxiang was advanced to Duke of Bao; and Sun Fangjian of Huazhou to Duke of Xiao.
The literal likewise renders 許州 as Xuzhou beside 徐州王晏. Xu Prefecture restores the distinction.
On bingxu Cangzhou military governor Zheng Renhui became military affairs commissioner and grand councilor;
On bingxu Chanzhou military governor Zheng Renhui became military affairs commissioner and grand councilor;
澶州節度使鄭仁誨 is Chanzhou, not Cangzhou (滄州), which appears later as Li Hui's posting.
On bingxu, Zheng Renhui, military governor of Cangzhou, was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and given concurrent Grand Councilor;
On bingxu, Zheng Renhui, military governor of Chanzhou, was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and given concurrent Grand Councilor;
The literal repeats Cangzhou for 澶州. Chanzhou is required.
Li Hui of Cangzhou was made acting grand general;
Li Hui of Cangzhou was made acting grand commandant;
滄州李暉加檢校太尉 confers Acting Grand Commandant, not grand general. Cangzhou itself is correctly 滄州 here.
Li Hui of Cangzhou was made Acting Grand General;
Li Hui of Cangzhou was made Acting Grand Commandant;
The literal makes the same 太尉 error for Li Hui.
Wang Rao of Beizhou was made acting grand general;
Wang Rao of Beizhou was made acting grand commandant;
貝州王饒加檢校太尉 is likewise Acting Grand Commandant, not grand general.
Wang Rao of Beizhou was made Acting Grand General;
